reasoning: FairTix operates an anti-bot ticketing platform with lottery-based fair queue systems, transparent pricing, and human verification. They have partially automated customer onboarding, lottery winner notifications, and support ticket handling. However, critical gaps exist: no payment processing automation, no ticket fulfillment workflows, no fraud detection systems, no analytics pipelines, and no integrations with payment providers or event management systems. The high error rates (36% for lottery notifications) and inactive status of revenue-critical workflows suggest operational issues. The company has built isolated automation islands without connecting the full customer journey from registration through ticket delivery.

nextMove.text: First, fix the lottery winner notification workflow's 36% failure rate by adding retry logic and switching to a transactional email service - this directly blocks revenue. Then build the payment processing automation since you can't capture revenue from notified winners without it. Finally, add ticket delivery automation to complete the core purchase flow. Only after this revenue pipeline works end-to-end should you enhance verification, analytics, and resale features.
nextMove.reasoning: Following the money: fix what's broken in the revenue path first (notifications), then fill the biggest gap (payments), then complete the customer journey (fulfillment). Everything else is optimization.
